public_rationale: This is a forecast that the generative AI race will never be winner-take-all. It has no deadline. Under the contract, it can be settled early only as contradicted, and only if dated evidence shows one country or firm has taken essentially the whole market and excluded its rivals. A forecast of this kind cannot be confirmed early. The only evidence is a TechCrunch report of a Menlo Ventures survey from July 2025, before the post (e1). It reports that Anthropic held 32% of enterprise LLM usage and OpenAI held 25%. That is a single snapshot and does not show what happens later. The packet contains no dated event that meets the early-contradiction rule, so the forecast stays open.
limitations: The only market data are a mid-2025 snapshot of enterprise LLM usage from before the post.
The packet does not say which countries the enterprise figures cover, and it has no data on Chinese providers or on use between countries.
The packet has no market data from after the December 2025 post.

our_interpretation: Read in context as mainly about the US-China race, and secondarily about firms.

criteria.support_condition: Over a long period, both countries and several firms keep large, lasting shares of generative AI use and supply, with no single winner pushing the other out.
criteria.contradiction_condition: One country or firm ends up with essentially the whole global generative AI market, excluding its rivals.
